Subject: MSA / Order Form — audit rights and pen test language

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for sending the draft MSA and order form. A couple quick asks from our side related to security exhibit / audit rights before we move to procurement:

- Can you confirm whether Redwood will allow a customer-led penetration test against our tenant (we'd run through your staging environment) or if you only allow vendor-led tests?
- We'd like a clearer cadence for SOC 2 evidence and attestations (how often Redwood will share refreshes, and what the expected turnaround is for specific evidence requests).
- Please confirm the scope for audit rights (who can visit/inspect, whether sampling is allowed, and any guardrails for multi-tenant systems).

We're targeting an internal purchasing committee review next week; if we can get proposed language and a short mutual action plan (timeline + owners), that will help.

Best,
Amelia

Head of Security Programs, WellSpring Health

Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — audit rights and pen test language

Amelia —

Thanks for the clear asks. I've looped in Laura (legal) and Ben (account lead) and will bring Soojin (security) and Karthik (product infra) into the thread for technical constraints. Quick operational plan attached — I put together a short action grid and a proposed set of redline suggestions for the security exhibit.

High-level answers up front:
- Pen tests: Redwood can support customer-run tests but we ask that they follow a bounded staging window and coordination flow (we do not allow unfettered production testing). We typically require a notice window and restricted scope — full details below in Soojin's note.
- SOC 2: We issue our SOC 2 Type II report annually and provide a security summary deck on request; for ad-hoc evidence requests we expect 3–5 business days for standard artifacts and will triage more complex asks with a traceable owner.
- Audit scope: We can accommodate inspection and evidence review under a defined inspection band (sampled, role-limited access). We aim to avoid privileged production inspections except in narrow, pre-agreed cases.

I attached a tracked redline (well_spring_msa_redline.docx) with recommended language for audit rights and a separate pen-test statement that reflects our staging-only policy. Please review and I'll set a short call to walk through.

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 3 Apr 2025 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA / Order Form — audit rights + proposed redlines

Amelia / Amanda —

Thanks for flagging — I reviewed the MSA and order form redlines Evelyn shared. Below are the substantive changes we recommend (high-level):

1) Inspection window and scope: we propose adding language that limits customer inspection to a mutually agreed period and a sampling approach — e.g., "inspection access to systems, logs, and artifacts shall be limited to non-production (staging) systems unless otherwise agreed in writing". This keeps tenant production systems out of scope by default.

2) Penetration testing: customer-led tests are permitted subject to a written test plan, minimum 10 business days' notice, non-disruptive rules of engagement, and execution only within staging or isolated test environments. We added a clause for immediate suspension rights if tests cause degradation.

3) Evidence cadence and emergency escalations: include a 3–5 business day SLA for standard SOC2 artifacts (configuration screenshots, policy extracts, procedure descriptions) and a definition for "complex" evidence requests that will require a longer timeline and a named Redwood owner.

4) Data handling during inspection: require that any data exported for review be limited to anonymized or redacted sets unless otherwise agreed under a separate DPA/amendment.

I've attached a tracked copy and included line-level comments. If these look acceptable to WellSpring we can convert to clean language and Ben can include the timeline in the mutual action plan.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: well_spring_msa_redline.docx (tracked comments)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 4 Apr 2025 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Technical constraints for pen tests and evidence requests

Amelia —

Quick technical clarifications to support Laura's redlines:

- Staging vs production: our staging environment mirrors production topology but is logically isolated. Customer tests must target the staging tenant we provide and cannot target live customer traffic or shared control-plane services.
- Test plan requirements: test scope, IP ranges, expected load profile, start/end times, and rollback/communication plan. We require a read-only snapshot of logs for triage; we will not provide raw production DB exports.
- Timing: we can support a single 3–5 day testing window per quarter for customer-initiated tests; additional windows can be scheduled but need business justification.
- Evidence handling: standard evidence package (SOC2 summary, control descriptions, configuration screenshots) can be shared within 3 business days. Anything requiring engineering traces or production logs is escalated and may take 7–10 business days.

I'll run a checklist with the ops team once we have a requested test plan. Happy to join a call to align on the technical gating.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Platform Security Operations, Redwood Inference
